transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... well... I guess I'm just having some trouble with... how I look. I can't really stop thinking about my hairline. And my face. I work at a restaurant, and under those lights, I just look... really old. And strange. 

I don't know. My coworkers tell me they don't see what I'm talking about, but... yeah. It's just hard to stop focusing on it. That's why I'm here.
How much distress would you say these thoughts about your hairline and face are causing you?
Um... I don't really know how to measure it. It's... it's a lot, I guess. I'm not really sure what else to say, it just... it really bothers me.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking the mirror or fixing your hair, because of these thoughts about your hairline and face?

Um... yeah. I suppose I do. 

Mostly before my shift starts. I'll just... I end up checking the bathroom mirror a lot. And I take pictures on my phone, just from different angles, to see how bad it looks. I keep combing my hair forward trying to fix it... and I just keep thinking about how the guests are going to see me when they walk up to the stand. 

Sometimes I get stuck doing it so long that I... I end up being late. Or I just get too worked up to even go out front. It's... yeah.
Do you find yourself worrying about your hairline and face when you're alone, or is it mostly when you're around other people or at work?

Um... I guess it's both. 

I mean, it's definitely worse when I'm at work... just knowing people are looking at me. But... yeah, I still think about it when I'm home alone. I don't really know. It just doesn't really go away.
Is it always your hairline and face that you're worried about, or are there other parts of your body that you also focus on?
Um... no. Not really. Just... just my hairline and my face. I don't really think about the rest of it.
Has your worry about your hairline and face affected your relationships with friends or family?

Um... yeah, I guess. I don't really see people much anymore. 

I stopped going on hikes with my friends... or to gallery events. I just... I can't handle people looking at me. I even skip the staff photos at work. 

And... well, work has been hard, too. I've been written up. Just... for being late, or missing shifts. Because I can't get past the mirror. So... yeah, it affects things.
Is it only how you look that's bothering you, or are you also worried about other things, like being judged or evaluated as a person?

Um... I don't know. I guess... it's just how I look. That's... that's the main thing. I just don't want them looking at my face or my hair. I don't really think about... the other stuff. Just the way I look.
Do you think your hairline and face would need to be completely perfect for you to stop worrying about them?
Um... I don't really know. I haven't thought about it having to be perfect. I just... I just don't want it to look the way it does. I'm not sure what it would take to stop worrying.
Have you had to turn down any social invitations or opportunities because of your concerns about your hairline and face?

Um... yeah. Like I was saying earlier... I just say no. To the hikes, or... the gallery events. If someone asks, I just don't go. I can't handle people seeing me like this. And... it's the same with work at the restaurant. Missing my shifts, or avoiding those staff photos... I just... I stay away. So, yeah. I turn them down.
Do you worry that people will judge you as a person, beyond just how you look, when they see your hairline and face?

Um... I think I mentioned this a minute ago... but no. I don't really think about... that part of it. It's just my face and my hair. I'm just worried about them seeing that. I don't really know about the rest.
Do you think you would stop worrying about your hairline and face if everyone around you told you they thought you looked fine?
Um... no. I don't think so. It wouldn't really matter what they said. I just... I know what I see in the mirror. So... no.
Is there something specific about your hairline or face that you think is particularly unattractive or problematic?

Um... well, I just... I can't stop thinking about it. It's mostly... how my hairline and my face look, especially under those bright lights at the restaurant. It just makes me look... old. And strange. My coworkers say they don't see what I'm talking about, but... yeah. That's what it is.
Do you think there's anything that could be done to your hairline or face that would make you stop worrying about how you look?
Um... I don't know. I haven't really... figured that out. I just know it looks bad. I don't know if anything would actually fix it.
Is there a particular feature of your face or hairline that you think is the most unattractive or problematic?
I just... I don't know. It's just... the whole thing. The way it all looks together. I can't really point to one specific thing, it's just... wrong.
Do you think you would still worry about yourself if you didn't worry about how you look?
I... I'm not really sure. I haven't... thought about it like that. This is just sort of... what takes up all my time. So... I don't know.
Do you think your appearance is actually as bad as you think it is, or is it just that you feel that way?
I... I don't really know how to answer that. I just... I see what I see. It's not just a feeling, it's... it's right there. So... I don't know.
Do you think other people see your hairline and face the same way you do?

I... I guess they say they don't. My coworkers, I mean. They tell me they don't see what I'm talking about. But... I just can't stop thinking about it anyway. It's... it's kind of why I'm here. 

Especially at work... the way my face and my hairline look under those restaurant lights... it just makes me look so old and... strange. So... I don't know what they actually see, but I can't stop focusing on it.
Do you think you would worry about what people think of you as a person if you didn't worry about your hairline and face?
I... I really couldn't say. I guess I just haven't ever pictured it. It's... hard to imagine not having this on my mind. So... I'm not sure.
Do you think you would still worry about yourself if your appearance was no longer a concern
I... I don't know. I can't really picture that. It's just... always there. I haven't really thought about what it would be like if it wasn't.
